text: 50-year-old female. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris.

The clinical picture of painful oral ulcers, genital dyspareunia, and blisters on the forearm, combined with your age and family history of autoimmune disorders, strongly suggests an autoimmune blistering disease rather than cellulitis. Although your previous physician suspected cellulitis, the presence of mucosal involvement and the specific distribution of lesions point toward Pemphigus Vulgaris. I recommend a skin biopsy for direct immunofluorescence to confirm this diagnosis.
